transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because people keep telling me I’m just imagining things, but I know what’s going on. The hospital people, and some people from the agency, they’ve been watching our house and even my cleaning routes. I think they’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.
Have you heard any voices or sounds that other people can't hear?
Yes. Sometimes when the house is quiet, I hear a woman’s voice by the kitchen window. It sounds real clear, like she’s standing right there, telling me to check the locks or move my husband’s pills.
Do you ever find it hard to understand what's real and what's not, or to connect your thoughts logically?

Yes, I guess so. When I try to explain what’s happening, it gets all mixed up. I’ll start talking about my husband’s heart pills, then I’m on the church schedule, then the numbers on my client list, and people tell me they can’t follow what I’m saying. It makes sense in my head, but it doesn’t always come out right.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words?

Yes. I try to say it straight, but my words jump around. I’ll be talking about my husband’s heart pills, then somehow I’m talking about the church schedule, then the numbers on my client list. People tell me they can’t follow what I’m saying, even though it feels connected to me.
Do you have trouble completing tasks or doing everyday activities because your thoughts are disjointed or you can't seem to stay on track?

Yes. It’s been affecting my work and home. My cleaning agency took away my supervisory routes because clients and coworkers said they couldn’t count on my work like before. And at home, my husband and my pastor have had to step in more, because I’m not keeping up with the caregiving and house responsibilities safely.
Do you believe these people from the hospital and agency are really watching you?

Yes. I know it sounds strange to people, but I do believe they’re watching. The hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes, like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.
Do you often have difficulty performing daily tasks in a logical order?

Yes, I do. I’ll start trying to do one thing, and then my thoughts don’t stay in order. Like when I’m explaining something, it jumps from my husband’s heart pills to the church schedule to numbers on my client list, and people tell me they can’t follow me. So yes, it makes it hard to go step by step.
Are the voices you hear or the people watching you the most disturbing or prominent part of your experience?

The voices are probably the most upsetting. Even when the house is quiet, I hear a woman’s voice near the kitchen window telling me to check the locks or move my husband’s pills. It sounds clear, like she’s standing right there, and it really shakes me.
Do you often find yourself doing things in a way that seems unusual or irrational to others?

Yes. I guess it does look strange to other people. At work or at home, I’ll start lining up bottles, towels, even chairs in certain patterns. Then I’ll walk back through the rooms again and again because it feels wrong to leave them any other way. I know people probably think it doesn’t make sense, but it feels like I have to do it.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, even when they don't seem necessary?

Yes. I’ll line things up—like bottles, towels, chairs—in a certain way, and then I keep walking back through the rooms to check it again. It doesn’t really need to be done, I know that, but it feels wrong to leave it any other way.
Do you feel anxious or fearful when you think about the hospital people and agency watching you?

Yes, I do. It makes me nervous and scared, because I feel like they’re watching our house and even my cleaning routes. They act like I’m making it up, but I know the hospital people and people from the agency are checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.
Do these experiences, like hearing voices or feeling like you're being watched, happen all the time or do they come and go?

They come and go, but it’s been going on for a long time now. The voices and that feeling like people are watching us… I’d say it’s been about 11 months. It’s not every single second, but it keeps coming back.
Do you have periods where none of these experiences, like the voices or feeling watched, happen at all?
Not really, no. They may not be happening every minute, but the voices and the feeling that people are watching us keep coming back. It’s been going on for about 11 months now.
Have these experiences affected your relationships with friends or family members?

Yes. It’s been hard on things at home and with work. My cleaning agency took away my supervisory routes because people were saying they couldn’t count on my work like before. And at home, my husband and my pastor have had to help more, because I haven’t been keeping up with the caregiving and house responsibilities the way I should, not safely all the time.
Do the voices you hear and the people you think are watching you seem to be part of a larger plan or story to you?

Yes… it does feel connected. I’m here because people keep saying I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. Like they’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.
Do the voices and the people watching you seem to be working together or have a common purpose?

Yes, that’s how it seems to me. Like they have the same purpose—to watch me and see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. I know people think I’m imagining it, but it feels like the hospital people and some people from the agency are connected in it.
Do the voices and the people watching you seem to fit into a single story or explanation that makes sense to you?

Yes. To me it all fits together. I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes. It’s like they’re trying to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.
Do the voices and the people watching you seem to be part of a story that makes sense to you, even if it doesn't to others?

Yes. I know it may not make sense to other people, but to me it does. The hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes, like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. That’s why I’m here—because everyone keeps saying I’m imagining it.
Do the voices and the people watching you seem to be connected by a single idea or belief that explains why they're doing these things?

Yes. The idea is that they think I’m not taking proper care of my husband. That’s why I’m here, because people keep saying I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house and my cleaning routes to check on me.
Do the voices and the people watching you seem to be connected by a single idea that explains everything?

Yes. It’s all the same thing to me. They think I’m not taking proper care of my husband, and that’s why the hospital people and people from the agency are watching our house and my cleaning routes. Everyone keeps saying I’m imagining it, but I know what’s happening.
